CBI Registers FIR in Disha Salian Death Case: Key Legal Observations
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has formally registered an FIR to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death of late Disha Salian, former manager of actor Sushant Singh Rajput.
Key Offences & Legal Framework Invoked
The FIR invokes critical provisions under the Indian Penal Code (IPC), reflecting major allegations:
Murder & Gang Rape: Severe substantive penal charges addressing non-bailable offences.
Criminal Conspiracy & Destruction of Evidence: Provisions addressing alleged procedural cover-ups, suppression, or tampering with material evidence.
Providing False Information: Legal implications pertaining to misdirection or incorrect reporting during earlier stages of investigation.
Entities Named & Institutional Scope
The FIR incorporates statements and allegations involving several high-profile individuals across political, administrative, and law enforcement spectrums:
Political & Public Figures: Former Chief Minister Uddhav Thackeray, Aaditya Thackeray, and former Home Minister Anil Deshmukh.
Law Enforcement & Administration: Former Mumbai Police Commissioner Param Bir Singh, Sachin Vaze, DCP Vishal Thakur, along with forensic officials and medical personnel.
Private Individuals: Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Rhea Chakraborty, Showik Chakraborty, and security staff.
Judicial & Investigative Trajectory
Evidentiary Threshold: Given the significant lapse of time since 2020, establishing a verifiable chain of custody for digital and physical evidence will be central to the investigation.
Naming vs. Indictment: In legal procedure, inclusion in an FIR serves as a basis for investigation into specific roles and does not constitute a finding of guilt or formal charge-sheeting until supported by material evidence.
Statutory Remedies: Named individuals retain the constitutional and statutory right to seek legal remedies, including anticipatory bail or petitions under Section 482 CrPC / Section 528 BNSS.
As the agency proceeds with its investigation, the legal fraternity will closely monitor the evidentiary submissions and adherence to procedural due process.
